INGLEWOOD  CALIFORNIA
  Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES November 7, 2019

A meeting of the Inglewood Park and Recreation Commission was convened on November 7,
2019, in Community Room A, located on the 1st floor of City Hall. Commissioner Willie Agee called
the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m. followed by the flag salute.

Roll Call

Present
  Commissioner Willie Agee, Chair - Commissioner at Large
  Commissioner Patricia Patrick, District One
  Commissioner Jacob Fragoso, District Two
  Commissioner Cynthia McLemore, District Three
  Commissioner Fernando Meza, District Four
  Sabrina Barnes, Director - Parks, Recreation and Community Services
  Teresa Estrada, Recreation Superintendent
  Thomas Uwal, Human Services Superintendent
  Gilbert Gonzalez, Graffiti Abatement Supervisor
  Stephanie Maldonado, Senior Management Assistant
Absent
  None

Public Comments

  None

Approval of the Minutes

  Commissioner Patrick made a motion to approve the minutes from October 3, 2019.
Commissioner McLemore seconded and the minutes were approved as follows:

  Ayes: Commissioners Patrick, Fragoso, Agee, McLemore and Meza
  Nays: None

Director’s Business

  Director Barnes presented a staff report recommending the Park and Recreation
Commission recommend the Mayor and Council Members approve a cooperative service
agreement with MDJ Management, LLC for resurfacing of two swimming pools at Edward Vincent
in accordance with the Sourcewell cooperative agreement in an amount not to exceed
$327,105.58. Edward Vincent, Jr. Park has a variety of amenities at the location which includes
lap pool and a wading pool. The pools were last resurfaced in 2003. In recent years, the City of
Inglewood has received reports of peeling, which is a potential safety hazard. We would like to
address this matter prior to the next swim season. The vendor chosen will provide special

  1
 INGLEWOOD  CALIFORNIA
  Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES November 7, 2019

surfacing (aqua glass) that has a 15 year warranty. They will provide new tile, swim lines and
markers. The project takes 3-4 weeks to complete. We anticipate completion in the first quarter of
the New Year. Commissioner Agee asked if the department has a definite start and completion
date. Director Barnes stated that there is no definite start date, but there is a tentative timeframe of
starting in March and completion by June. Commissioner Agee asked if the sides of the pool will
be resurfaced as well the pumps being replaced. Director Barnes stated that the entire pool will be
resurfaced as well as the wading pool. She also stated that the workers are being trained on how
to maintain the pumps.

  Commissioner Patrick moved to approve the staff report recommending the Mayor and
Council Members approve a cooperative service agreement with MDJ Management, LLC for
resurfacing of two (2) swimming pools at Vincent Park in accordance with the Source Well
cooperative agreement in an amount not to exceed $327,105.58. The staff report was approved as
follows:

  Ayes: Commissioners Patrick, Fragoso, Agee, McLemore and Meza
  Nays: None

Verbal Reports

  Gilbert Gonzalez gave a verbal report on behalf of the Parks Administration regarding the
following:
   The Park Maintenance staff is currently working with the Inglewood Baseball Fund and the
  construction of the baseball has begun. The funder will have a press conference on
  December 4th and a Community event on the following Sunday.
   Graffiti: The Division has had a busy month with increased activity in District 1, District 4
  and at Darby and Vincent Parks.

  Teresa Estrada gave a verbal report on behalf of the Recreation Division regarding the
following:
   The City of Inglewood has partnered with the Los Angeles Rams. They provided uniforms
  for all of the youth and the coaches. They provided training through Positive Coaching
  Alliance for the youth and their parents. They also held a Rams Community Day.
   The Inglewood Police Department is coaching three (3) teams this year. They are
  providing mentoring along with coaching the youth.
   Holiday Craft Workshop is being offered $5 per student. On Saturday December 12th from
  10-12 PM.
   Thursday December 5, 2020 is the Holiday Tree Lighting Ceremony at Inglewood City Hall.

  Sabrina Barnes informed the Commissioners that she did follow-up with Mr. Asfal regarding his
request for more time on the field. It was determined that their paperwork was not turned in on
time. We were able to accommodate them with more time on the field.

  2
 INGLEWOOD  CALIFORNIA
  Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES November 7, 2019

  Thomas Uwal gave a verbal report on behalf of the Human Services Division regarding the
following:
   The New Inglewood paratransit buses arrived last month with the two larger buses
  expected to follow in the month of December 2019. We are the final phases of installing
  the radios. The new buses are expected to be on the road this month. We are planning to
  show the new buses to the seniors at the Inglewood Senior Center prior to having them on
  the road.
   Mental health team from LA County (GENESIS & FACTS) will be starting monthly mental
  health one on one sessions with our seniors at the Inglewood Senior Center every first
  Thursday of the month, from 12:30 PM to 2:30 PM, starting Thursday, 11/7/19.
   A special Thanksgiving meal will be served on 11/20/19, including cranberry juice, freshly
  cooked roast turkey, dinner roll, cornbread stuffing, peas & carrots, mashed potatoes,
  green salad and pumpkin cake.
   Our fall bridge program this year will take place from November 25-27, 2019 from 7:30 AM-
  6:00PM at Darby Park. Parents can drop off their children at 7:30 AM and pick them up at
  6:00 PM the program will offer breakfast and lunch. The cost is only $60 per participant.

  Commissioner McLemore asked if there is a Thanksgiving food drive where can goods can be
donated. Mr. Uwal stated that a food drive is in discussion.

Director’s Report

  Sabrina Barnes gave an update on the following Capital Improvement Projects:
   The Tennis Courts at Edward Vincent Park were recently re-opened. The tennis courts
  was a renovation project that cost $3.25 million dollars.
   The RFP for Rogers Park Bathroom renovation has gone out. We’ve elected to have the
  vault system for the style of restrooms.
   We propose to go to Council mid-November for the resurfacing of the Pools at Edward
  Vincent Park. The resurfacing will cost about $350,000. The work will start around
  February 2020.
   We have ordered the nets for Pickle Ball at North Park.
   The HVAC system and windows at the Willie Agee Playhouse are on the list of upgrades.

  Commissioner Agee asked if a contractor has been picked for the pool resurfacing. Sabrina
Barnes stated we are in the bidding process. He also stated that he enjoyed the tennis court
reopening. Commissioner Agee asked for a list of ten items that was created based on the original
survey from years prior. Ms. Barnes stated that the list is in the last agenda packet. The staff will
resend the packet out to the Commissioners. Ms. Barnes reiterated that the air conditioning was
approved for the Willie Agee Playhouse.

  3

  MINUTES November 7, 2019

Public Comments

  None

Commissioner Comments

  All of the Commissioners thanked staff for their reports and hard work.

With no further comments the meeting was adjourned at 6:48 p.m.
